snack.en: Is it: a) crisps, b) confectionary and chocolate, or c) savoury snacks and biscuits?
snack.zh: 是：a) 薯片，b) 糖果和巧克力，还是 c) 咸味小吃和饼干？

snack.en: Barbara wants her son to eat healthy, homemade food, although he prefers modern, packaged snacks.
snack.zh: Barbara 希望她的儿子吃健康的自制食物，尽管他更喜欢现代包装零食。

snack.en: A good way of finding out about British tastes is with the nation's best-loved snack, crisps.
snack.zh: 了解英国人口味的一个好方法，就是看看这个国家最受欢迎的零食——薯片。

snack.en: I usually go to the supermarket when I'm hungry, so I end up buying lots of snacks.
snack.zh: 我通常饿着肚子去超市，结果买了一大堆零食。

snack.en: For one, give children a choice – for example, by offering small, healthy snacks and dips before the meal.
snack.zh: 首先，给孩子一个选择——例如，在饭前提供小份的健康零食和蘸酱。

snowy.en: All of them came from the snowy and mountainous regions of Japan.
snowy.zh: 他们全都来自日本多雪和多山的地区。

snowy.en: But seen from a distance in the snowy mountain forests where they live, black and white makes the perfect disguise.
snowy.zh: 但如果从它们居住的白雪皑皑的山林远眺，黑白两色就成了完美的伪装。

sneeze.en: But first, Georgie, a question. We all know the common cold – now, that’s the illness that makes you cough and sneeze, have a sore throat and headache.
sneeze.zh: 但首先，Georgie，有个问题。我们都知道普通感冒——也就是那种让你咳嗽、打喷嚏、喉咙痛和头疼的疾病。

snake.en: And that image of an eagle and a snake is now in the middle of Mexico’s national flag.
snake.zh: 而那只老鹰和蛇的图案如今就印在墨西哥国旗的正中央。

snake.en: According to Aztec legend, their gods told them to build a city where they see an eagle eating a snake while standing on a cactus.
snake.zh: 根据阿兹特克传说，他们的神明告诉他们，要在他们看到一只老鹰站在仙人掌上吃蛇的地方建立城市。

snake.en: From the early morning, up and down the country, queues snaked around the block as people waited in line for their chance to read what promised to be a bombshell story.
snake.zh: 从清晨开始，全国各地排起了长龙，人们排队等待机会阅读一篇注定会引发轰动的故事。

snake.en: So during the spring and autumn equinoxes, which is when the day and night are equal, the sunlight creates a shadow on the staircase that resembles a serpent, a snake, moving down the pyramid.
snake.zh: 所以在春分和秋分时节，即昼夜平分的时候，阳光在阶梯上投下阴影，看起来就像一条巨蛇正在顺着金字塔往下爬。

snake.en: In one display of particularly creative military thinking, in a battle between two naval powers in modern-day Turkey, he advised for poisonous snakes to be put into clay pots and then thrown onto the enemy ship, the logic being that soldiers on ships don’t tend to wear many clothes, and they can’t exactly run away, so having hundreds of angry poisonous snakes slithering around is pretty much any sailor’s worst nightmare.
snake.zh: 在展示其极具创意的军事思维时，有一次在现代土耳其境内的一场两国海军之战中，他建议将毒蛇装进陶罐里，然后扔到敌舰上。其逻辑是：战舰上的水兵们通常穿得比较少，而且在船上也无处可逃，因此有成百上千条愤怒的毒蛇在身边滑来滑去，绝对是任何水手挥之不去的噩梦。

snatch.en: To the 500 or so Puritans huddled in their icy wooden homes, he was an ever-present enemy, lurking in the shadows, waiting to snatch their souls.
snatch.zh: 对于挤在冰冷木屋里的那大约500名清教徒来说，他是无处不在的敌人，潜伏在阴影中，随时准备夺走他们的灵魂。

snatch.en: He turned around to see what was going on, and before he knew it, he had been bustled to the ground, his laptop snatched away before he had time to close the screen or press the keyboard shortcut to delete everything.
snatch.zh: 他转过身想看看发生了什么，还没等他反应过来，他就被按倒在地上，笔记本电脑也被夺走了，他根本来不及合上屏幕或按下快捷键来删除一切。

snob.en: And he considers Southern men to be snobs, doing easy work.
snob.zh: 而他认为南方男人是势利眼，干着轻松的差事。

snob.en: And then the BBC journalist went to the north to ask the northerners about their view of the south, and they responded that Southerners are snobs, they go out to eat at restaurants because they can’t cook for themselves, and that they wouldn’t even dream of living in the south because it sounds so awful.
snob.zh: 接着，BBC 记者去北方询问北方人对南方的看法，他们回答说南方人都是势利眼，他们去餐馆吃饭是因为自己不会做饭，而且北方人做梦都没想到过去南方生活，因为南方听起来太糟糕了。

snap.en: Patterns, and as you said, games of snap, where you don't even realize you're now just reacting.
snap.zh: 模式，正如你所说的，像玩‘拍手游戏’一样，你甚至没有意识到自己只是在做出反应。

snap.en: And then kind of matching the cards. There's this game where you match the cards together and go snap.
snap.zh: 我真正了解自己是在成年后通过我的触发点。

snap.en: And just something one day just fucking snapped.
snap.zh: 有一天，某样东西突然断了。

sneak.en: Brilliant. So Christopher Hitchens, one of the new atheists, was sat in some British pub with Douglas Murray when Douglas is young and you know you can imagine it's some musty Chesterfield sofa he's probably got a cigarette in his mouth and a glass of scotch or something and uh Douglas is vacillating between these two different choices that he needs to make and he is um complaining lamenting the fact that I have this thing but I have this thing and if I do this thing I can't do this thing and and what what do i do and apparently hitch like sat back and douglas in life we must choose our regrets and i was like fuck so i'm three manhattans deep in douglas murray's apartment in manhattan at two in the morning and he sneaks off to the toilet and i quickly write this down because i know that my like half cut alcohol brain isn't going to remember it so i've noted down.
sneak.zh: 太精彩了。克里斯托弗·希钦斯，新无神论者之一，有一次在一家英国酒吧里，和年轻时的道格拉斯·穆雷坐在一起，你可以想象那是一个发霉的切斯特菲尔德沙发，他嘴里可能叼着一支烟，手里端着一杯苏格兰威士忌什么的，然后啊，道格拉斯正在他需要做出的两个不同选择之间举棋不定，他正在，呃，抱怨、哀叹着说：我既有这个机会，又有那个机会，如果我选了这个，就没法选那个，然后，我到底该怎么办啊？据说希钦往后一靠，说道：“道格拉斯，在生活中，我们必须选择我们的遗憾。”我当时想：我靠！当时我在曼哈顿道格拉斯·穆雷的公寓里，已经喝了三杯曼哈顿鸡尾酒，时间是凌晨两点，他悄悄溜去洗手间，我赶紧把这话记下来，因为我知道我那半醉的酒精大脑根本记不住，所以我把它记了下来。
